newsitem.title: ITALY: Privatisation revenue could help Italy in EMU - IMI.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation revenue could help Italy in EMU - IMI.

text.p: Privatisations are a "necessary but insufficient" condition to restore Italian state finances to health and a "more significant recourse" to state sell-offs could contribute to Italy's stable entry into a single European currency, director-general of IMI bank Rainer Masera said.
He put a value of 300 trillion lire on privatisations to be carried out in the next three to five years, including utilities, banks and real estate owned by the state.

Speaking at a presentation of a new book on stock markets, he suggested the method of debt equity swaps could be used more whereby state debt instruments are made convertible to purchase shares in privatised companies.

He warned against a slowdown in the government's privatisation programme which, including the just announced second tranche flotation of some 10 percent in state-controlled energy group ENI, will have brought some 40 trillion lire into the state coffers.
